newsitem.title: UK: Eurobond trade ideas - Anomaly in Eurodollars.
newsitem.headline: Eurobond trade ideas - Anomaly in Eurodollars.

text.p: Eurobond analysts' latest Eurobond trade ideas focused on Euromarks, Eurodollars, Euroyen and Eurolire.
Tokyo-Mitsubishi International recommend an anomaly opportunity in the Toyota 6.5 percent May 2001 Eurodollar bond.
The generally steep curve up to five years means bonds with a maturity of less than five years show good "roll-down characteristics," Tokyo-Mitsubishi said.
The two- to five- year U.S. Treasury spread has widened to 33 b.p. from 24 b.p. since December 1996.
Sanwa International recommend a Euromark lengthening switch into the 5.75 percent Spain January 2007 bond out of the 7.0 percent Spain bond due January 2000.
Weak demand in the German construction sector could lead to a 0.75 percent fall in long-term mortgage rates, a Bundesbank council member said on Tuesday.
Sanwa say that there is a strong correlation between mortgage rates and Bunds so these remarks in principle should help the long-end.
Following are latest trade ideas, compiled by Reuters:
EUROMARK
Sanwa International recommends:
BUY Spain 5.75 pct 01/07
SELL Spain 7.0 pct 01/00
STRATEGY This switch gives a 197 b.p. pick-up in yield
providing for a wide cost of carry. The buy side of the switch can also be bought below par (22.Jan.97) and the sell side can be sold at a significnat premium to par.
EURODOLLARS
Paribas Capital Markets recommends:
BUY KFW 8.25 PCT 11/04
SELL Finland 7.875 pct 07/04
STRATEGY This switch offers a 5 b.p. pick up in yield and
an improvement in credit quality while only moving out by four months along the yield curve.
There has been an improving investor perception towards Finnish eurobonds which has tightened the spread trend over the last few months.
Tokyo-Mitsubishi International recommend:
BUY Toyota 6.5 pct 05/01
STRATEGY Launched in May 1996 the spread is still over the
five-year benchmark but the bond is gradually rolling down the curve and is soon likely to be spread over three-year Treasuries.

It currently trades around 3 b.p. through the five-year Treasury, or 2 b.p. over the interpolated curve. This equates to 18 b.p. over the current three-year or 15 bp. over the fourthcoming three-year Treasury in February.
BUY Credit Local 6.875 PCT 06/01
STRATEGY This buy is subject to the same reasoning as
above. The bond yields 14 b.p over the current five-year on the offer, which equates to 33 b.p. over the three-year.
EUROYEN
Yamaichi recommends:
BUY Export Import Bank of Japan 2.875 pct 2005
SELL Japan Development Bank 6.50 pct 2001
STRATEGY This switch will give a pick-up in yield of 95
b.p. compared with around 90 b.p. at the end of last year.
EUROLIRE
San Paolo recommends:
BUY EIB 9.60 pct 01/01
SELL EIB 7.55 pct 11/01
STRATEGY This switch gives around 14 b.p. pick-up in

yield. The sell side of the switch is expensive against the swap and BTP trading at 48 b.p. and 34 b.p. through respectively. The EIB 9.60 pct bond is cheap for a supranational trading at 18 b.p. through the swap (offer side) and 22 through the BTP (offer side).
BUY World Bank 7.625 pct 11/03
SELL World Bank 9.45 pct 08/03
STRATEGY The move into the World Bank 7.625 pct bond
offers about a 9 b.p. pick-up in yield and trades at a lower premium. It is cheap against the swap at 18 b.p. through and the BTP at 29 b.p. through.
